consensus_summary: Babel/Babylon is the archetypal symbol of human pride, self-exaltation, and organized rebellion against God—the idolatrous, oppressive ‘city of man’ or godless world system/empire opposed to God’s kingdom and destined for judgment.
book_summary: The self-made kingdom that builds a name against heaven—an empire raised over many kingdoms, the covenant counterfeit.
consensus_core_identification: archetypal prideful anti-God world empire/system (city of man vs. city of God)
book_core_identification: self-made kingdom/empire building a name against heaven and counterfeiting the covenant
rationale: Minimum cores are equivalent: both identify Babel/Babylon as the self-exalting human kingdom/empire that rebels against heaven and stands as the anti-God system. The book’s compact phrasing (‘builds a name against heaven,’ ‘empire raised over many kingdoms,’ ‘covenant counterfeit’) is a stylistic restatement of the same referent already present in the consensus primary (pride/name-making from Gen 11, imperial rule from Rev 17, counterfeit of God’s city/kingdom). Extra detail does not alter category, replace the referent, or reclassify cases; alternatives listed in the consensus remain secondary for both.
strongest_objection: The term ‘covenant counterfeit’ could be read as introducing a slightly more precise covenantal framing than the broad consensus always states explicitly, though it remains fully compatible and does not change the core identification.
